origin.description: Concatenates character vectors element by element. stri_c and stri_paste are the same function.
origin.usage: stri_join(..., sep = "", collapse = NULL, ignore_null = FALSE)

arguments.text: Character vectors, or objects coercible to character vectors, concatenated element by element.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: A single string placed between the vectors. Only the first element is used.

arguments.name: collapse
arguments.text: NULL, or a single string placed between the rows.

arguments.name: ignore_null
arguments.text: If TRUE, length-zero arguments are ignored.

origin.details: The result length is the longest argument. collapse joins those rows into one string. A length-zero argument makes the result empty when ignore_null is FALSE, and is dropped when ignore_null is TRUE. If every argument is dropped, collapse NULL gives an empty vector and a collapse string gives one empty string. sep and collapse longer than one use the first string and warn. A missing value in a row makes that row missing. With collapse set, any missing row makes the one result missing. paste would have inserted the letters NA instead. One vector does not insert sep; a collapse string is then stri_flatten. An empty sep with two vectors concatenates each pair.
origin.value: A character vector. With collapse set, it has length one.

translation.description: Concatenates vectors element by element. stri_c and stri_paste are the same function.

arguments.name: args
arguments.text: Strings, numbers, logicals, NA, None, or lists of those. None is an empty vector. A Python int is formatted as an R integer and a float as an R double.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: String placed between the vectors. None is rejected. Only the first element of a list is used.

arguments.name: collapse
arguments.text: None leaves a vector. A string joins the rows. NA makes the result missing once there is something to join.

arguments.name: ignore_null
arguments.text: If true, length-zero arguments are dropped.

translation.details: The result length is the longest argument. collapse joins those rows into one string. A length-zero argument makes the result empty when ignore_null is FALSE, and is dropped when ignore_null is TRUE. If every argument is dropped, collapse NULL gives an empty vector and a collapse string gives one empty string. sep and collapse longer than one use the first string and warn. A missing value in a row makes that row missing. With collapse set, any missing row makes the one result missing. paste would have inserted the letters NA instead. One vector does not insert sep; a collapse string is then stri_flatten. An empty sep with two vectors concatenates each pair. A missing character is NA, not the string NA.
translation.value: A list of strings. A collapsed result is a one-element list.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA
from stringi.join import stri_join
print(stri_join([1, 2, 3], ["a", "b", "c"], sep="-"))
